title: Reading the board before you act
target: How to read the board in the card game in TCG Card Shop Simulator before committing to a play, so a turn is decided from what is on the table rather than from memory.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A play table with a game in progress
A deck you are playing with
Some idea of what your cards do

steps.do: Read attack as three totals rather than one number.
steps.because: the board keeps a base attack list and two separate boost lists, one for the elements involved and one for cards (m_AtkPowerList, m_BoostElementAtkPowerList, m_BoostCardAtkPowerList)

steps.do: Put a card where the elements can add to it.
steps.because: the board holds positions and card lists for the element areas, and tracks which area you are hovering by index (m_ElementAreaPosList, m_ElementAreaCardList, m_CurrentHoverElementAreaIndex)

steps.do: Check the guardian row before you commit an attacker.
steps.because: guardians have their own positions and their own list of cards (m_GuardianCardPosList, m_GuardianCard3dList)

steps.do: Watch both ends of the deck, not only the top.
steps.because: the deck is kept as a top list and a bottom list (m_TopDeckCard3dList, m_BottomDeckCard3dList)

steps.do: Read the discard pile before you decide what is gone.
steps.because: the pile has its own position and card lists, and the board remembers the cards discarded most recently (m_DiscardPosList, m_DiscardCard3dList, m_LastTriggerDiscardedCard3dList)

steps.do: Wait for a resolution to finish rather than starting another.
steps.because: the board keeps the cards selected for a resolution, the cards valid for it and a flag for a turn waiting to resolve (m_ResolveActionSelectedCardList, m_ResolveActionValidCardList, m_IsWaitingActionResolve)

steps.do: Know that a resolution can refuse to repeat a kind of monster.
steps.because: there is a list to check against and a list of the kinds already chosen (m_ActionResolveMonsterTypeNoRepeatCheckList, m_ActionResolveMonsterTypeSelectedList)

steps.do: Know which areas are occupied before you plan around them.
steps.because: the board remembers the monsters standing in the element areas (m_ElementAreaMonsterDataList)

commonMistakes: Adding up one attack number and forgetting the element and card boosts.
Attacking past a guardian because you did not look at the row.
Planning around the top of the deck and forgetting that cards can go under it.
Acting again while a resolution is still waiting.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
